s1.syndrome_frame: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Systemic symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
Presence of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
key_facts: 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Symptoms duration of 1 month
Previous medical history of elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Laboratory tests were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

raw.syndrome_frame: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Systemic symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
Presence of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
key_facts: 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Symptoms duration of 1 month
Previous medical history of elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Laboratory tests were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, is most consistent with a diagnosis of Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can present with extranodal involvement, including skin lesions.

rejected.label: Burkitt lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and often involves the jaw, abdomen, or other sites, rather than a localized skin lesion.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with multiple lesions and has a more indolent course, with a different immunophenotypic profile.

rejected.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with nasal or other extranodal involvement and has a distinct immunophenotypic profile, including positivity for CD56 and negativity for CD20.

rejected.label: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more indolent course, with lymphocytosis and involvement of the bone marrow, spleen, and lymph nodes, rather than a localized skin lesion.
